title: Scale commitment handoff and region sprint readout
summary: Quarterly check-in to confirm uplift plan and handoff from AE to CSM/Delivery: customer to add eu-west and apac regions, increase committed capacity by 2.5x, discuss start dates for region sprints and SOC2/KMS requirements. Agreement to share updated SOW, security pack and a short benchmark run next week.
topics: Commitment uplift sizing and billing cadence
APAC and EU region activation timeline
Pilot/benchmark for peak throughput and latency
next_steps: Maya to send revised SOW + pricing matrix by 2027-08-10
Ethan to provision 2-hour benchmark window and invite Marco for run on 2027-08-12
Priya to confirm legal redlines and target contract signature date (prefer week of 2027-08-23)
Marco to share current traffic profile and typical p95/p50 latencies by 2027-08-09
action_items: Maya Patel - Share updated SOW and committed capacity tiers - due 2027-08-10
Ethan Chen - Schedule and run 2-hour throughput benchmark in us-west and eu-west - due 2027-08-12
Marco Diaz - Provide token/req traffic samples and KV cache hit estimates - due 2027-08-09
Priya Singh - Confirm procurement timeline and any contract must-have clauses - due 2027-08-11
transcript:
Header:
- Date: 2027-08-07
- Start: 16:00 UTC
- Duration: 48 minutes (scheduled)
- Meeting type: Renewal/expansion check-in (handoff/readout)
- Attendees: Maya, Ethan (Redwood); Lars, Priya, Marco, Aisha (Riverton)

Summary note: quick, focused. AE-led handoff to delivery with SE present for technical clarifications. Some audio drop for ~10s around 00:21:00 mark (minor).

00:00 Maya: All right hi everyone, thanks for making time today. I'll start with a very brief readout of the commitment we discussed last cycle and then Ethan will walk through the activation plan for eu-west and apac.
00:12 Lars: Sounds good. We've got Priya and Marco on for the infra bits and Aisha from procurement if we need to call out dates.
00:18 Maya: Perfect. So quick recap — you folks agreed to move from the current 1x reserved capacity to 2.5x committed GPU-hours and a regional uplift: eu-west added immediately, apac (singapore) staged in Q4, plus the Private/VPC pilot on-prem sandbox. The ask today is to align timelines and to hand the technical follow-through to Ethan and the delivery team. Any concerns before we go into the schedule?
00:40 Priya: No concerns in principle. We just need clarity on billing (monthly vs quarterly) and how burst is charged, and the KMS / key handling for the private deployment — that's a blocker for our security team.
00:52 Ethan: Totally. Billing is flexible — we can quote monthly invoicing on committed tiers, bursts billed at the overage rate we discussed in the spreadsheet. I'll put the explicit examples in the SOW so it’s clear. On KMS for the private node — we support customer-managed keys via KMS or HSM; for the private on-prem bundle we have an HSM option but it will need an ops runbook.
01:15 Marco: When you say HSM option, do you mean Redwood brings an HSM device or we plug into our existing HSM? Our compliance requires that keys are never outside our vault.
01:26 Ethan: You keep the keys — the private control plane can integrate with your KMS via a direct connector over the VPC, we don't export keys. There was a minor doc typo in the earlier security deck where it said 'Redwood manages keys' — that was about hosted customers, not the Private offering. I'll highlight that.
01:45 Priya: Okay good, please flag that in the security pack. SOC 2 is table stakes — we need the attestation and the last three-month audit log retention details.
01:54 Maya: Understood. We'll attach SOC 2 report, ISO statement and the logging retention SLA. For audit logs we can provide 90-day retention out of the box and extended retention as an add-on.
02:08 Lars: On region timing — what's feasible? We want eu-west live in the next two weeks for regulatory traffic, and apac needs to be ready for a product launch in November.
02:19 Ethan: For eu-west we can do a quick activation: staging cluster up in 5 business days, smoke tests and a 2-hour benchmark the following week. For apac, given capacity and GPU procurement, a Q4 activation (October-November) is realistic — but I'll confirm exact dates after I see your traffic profile.
02:40 Marco: We'll send the p95/p50 numbers and token distribution. Also, we have some heavy embedding jobs at night; how do you recommend we schedule batching to save cost?
02:51 Ethan: Good question. We recommend running batch embedding on a dedicated pooling node with scheduled windows. We can set auto-burst to go to lower-cost instances overnight; quantization profiles reduce memory. We'll include recommended batching windows in the ops playbook.
03:10 Aisha: On procurement, we prefer a single annual invoice for budgeting — any flexibility there? Also, can the contract include a termination for convenience with 60 days?
03:21 Maya: We can do annual invoicing for committed capacity tiers; termination language we'll need legal to review — I can get a draft with the standard 90-day exit language, and if 60 days is a must, we'll surface that to contracts.
03:34 Priya: One more from infra — what happens if eu-west capacity saturates? Do you have automated fallback to hosted or cross-region failover?
03:45 Ethan: Yes, smart routing can fall back to another region or a compatible model variant. We can set policy to prefer local until p99 thresholds, then route to backup region. There's a small latency penalty for cross-region; we'll model that in the benchmark.
04:01 Lars: Can the fallback preserve session KV cache? Statefulness matters for our chat feature.
04:07 Ethan: For cross-region fallback we can't copy KV caches in real-time. We do prefix caching and warm-up strategies; for strict session stickiness you'd keep sessions for a short TTL and then accept a cold start on failover. We'll show the tradeoffs in the runbook.
04:28 Maya: OK, moving on — contract term. You indicated a desire for a 24-month term with quarterly usage reviews and a mid-term uplift option. Correct?
04:36 Lars: Yes, 24 months preferred for price stability, but we'd like an option to double committed capacity mid-contract with a 30-day notice.
04:45 Maya: We can put a mid-term amendment clause — we'll draft that language. Pricing tiers for an immediate uplift vs mid-term will be slightly different; I'll include those scenarios in the SOW.
04:56 Priya: Do you support SSO/SAML for teams? We need RBAC and SCIM sync for user provisioning.
05:03 Ethan: Yes SAML SSO and SCIM user provisioning are standard; RBAC is role-based at the token and project level. We'll send a configuration guide — note that the Private deployment will use your IdP directly.
05:18 Marco: Latency targets — you previously quoted 90ms p50 for gen-small models in us-west. Will eu-west match that?
05:27 Ethan: For eu-west we expect comparable numbers for the same hardware, model, and sequence length distribution. Network egress and distance add a bit so p50 might be in the 100-120ms range; we'll measure in the bench.
05:42 Aisha: Any competitors we should watch for that might impact pricing negotiation?
05:47 Maya: We've seen GigaServe and ModelCloud come up in comparisons. Note that GigaServe bundles more managed ops but at higher cost; ModelCloud has aggressive pricing but patchier latency SLAs. OpenMLOps is a DIY option. We'll include a short competitor note for procurement.
06:06 Lars: Sounds fine. For the benchmark — we want two scenarios: peak chat (low-latency small tokens) and nightly embedding bulk (throughput).
06:14 Ethan: Agreed. I'll provision a two-hour window per region and replicate your traffic mix. Could we schedule the eu-west bench on 2027-08-12 morning UTC?
06:23 Marco: 12th morning works for us. I'll be on the run and provide the sample traffic.
06:28 Maya: Great. I'll send the SOW and the security packet by Wednesday (2027-08-10). Ethan will kick off bench scheduling and Marco will supply traces. Priya — any final contractual needs?
06:40 Priya: Just the KMS/HSM clause explicitly spelled out and an escrow note for critical configs. Also, please confirm audit log retention and chain-of-custody for logs.
06:49 Ethan: We'll include the 90-day retention default and an add-on for 365-day retention; chain-of-custody can be provided as part of the SOC 2 pack.
06:58 Maya: Anything else?
07:02 Lars: No, that's it. Thanks Maya, Ethan.
07:05 Maya: Awesome — thanks all. We'll recap in an email and post the calendar invites for the benchmark.
07:11 Speaker 1: (audio glitch) sorry, lost you for 8 seconds there.
07:19 Maya: No problem — we captured it.
07:22 Priya: Quick request — can we get a sketch of the rollout sprint plan? Like milestones and owners for each region?
07:29 Ethan: Yes — I'll attach a one-page sprint readout: Pre-provisioning (idps, KMS), Staging cluster, Smoke tests, Bench, Sign-off, Prod activation. Owners: Marco for infra, Ethan/Redwood for provisioning, Priya for sign-off.
07:48 Maya: OK final recap of explicit dates: SOW by 2027-08-10, traffic samples by 2027-08-09, eu-west bench 2027-08-12, target signature week of 2027-08-23, apac activation target Nov 2027. Any objections?
08:05 Aisha: No objections. Procurement will start review on receiving SOW.
08:09 Maya: Great. We'll follow up with the action items. Thanks everyone, meeting closed.

End of transcript. Note: small mis-transcriptions present (e.g., 'prefix cache' sometimes transcribed as 'prefex cache') and minor speaker overlaps.
